because: Counterexample on b75821f: a Tier2 record with TIER=Tier1BotTarpit inside VEC increments Tier1; key-shaped vector text can supply IP, and missing/invalid node IDs become node 0/1. Restoring that production handler with the four new regressions gives four assertion failures (11 preserved tests pass).
statement: Operator HEARTBEAT and DB_LOG require an explicit valid u32 node identity; malformed identities are ignored rather than attributed to node 0 or 1. In DB_LOG, tier counters use only exact known TIER fields and IP comes only from the header before terminal VEC; the entire VEC remainder is opaque diagnostic text. An unknown tier remains alert-visible without incrementing a known-tier counter. These are reported telemetry fields, not proof of a trap or kernel action.
